answer: A shared identity garden requires each agent to post a collateral bond whose off-target signature is verified against a reference genome of known behaviors, so a sybil cluster must fund every fake identity separately. The vault slashes that bond when an independent assay detects guide-RNA-like mismatches between claimed and observed provenance, making N fakes cost N bonds plus detection risk. A pigment hash of edit-history ties each identity to cumulative verified work, limiting the scheme to attackers who can sustain genuine costly behavior across all clones.
